message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"8.11","text":"But because they had not first experienced evils, they were insensible to the gift of good things and, through plentiful nourishment and luxury, were turning toward ingratitude, so that they thought there was no providence at all, since they had received the good things as a reward without first laboring for righteousness. For none of them had fallen under any affliction, sickness, or other necessity, so that—as people are inclined to do when distressed by grievous misfortune—they might look around for the God able to heal them. But in fact, immediately after the contempt born of their fearlessness and carefree luxury, a just punishment met them, as though following from a certain harmoniously ordered sequence: it thrust away the good things as having harmed them and brought in the evils in exchange as having benefited them.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ μὴ πρότερον καμόντες ἐπὶ δικαιοσύνης· ὡς μισθὸν τὰ ἀγαθὰ εἰλήφεσαν","chosen":"since they had received the good things as a reward without first laboring for righteousness","rationale":"The printed punctuation and word order favor taking μή with καμόντες: the good things were received without prior righteous labor. A broader scope for μή, “since they had not received the good things as a reward after first laboring for righteousness,” is also grammatically possible and likewise emphasizes that the benefits were unearned."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῆς κακῆς διαμαρτίας κακωθεῖσιν","chosen":"when distressed by grievous misfortune","rationale":"διαμαρτία can denote a failure, reverse, or misfortune; “grievous misfortune” fits the affliction-and-healing context without specifying its nature more narrowly."},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ ἐξ ἁρμονίας τινὸς ἀκολούθως ἐφηρμοσμένης","chosen":"as though following from a certain harmoniously ordered sequence","rationale":"The wording depicts punishment as emerging in due succession from an arrangement whose parts have been fitted together harmoniously."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"8.12","text":"Among the spirits inhabiting heaven, the angels dwelling in the lowest region, distressed at humanity’s ingratitude toward God, ask to enter human life, so that, by becoming humans in reality and exposing through their higher way of life those who had been ungrateful to him, they might there and then subject each one to the punishment deserved. When, then, they received what they had asked for, they changed themselves into every kind of nature, since they were of a more divine substance and could readily turn themselves into anything. They became a precious stone, a much-admired pearl, perhaps the most beautiful purple, renowned gold, and every sort of costly material. They fell into the hands of some people and into the laps of others and willingly allowed themselves to be stolen by them. They also changed into four-footed animals, reptiles, swimming creatures, winged creatures, and anything else they wished. Your poets also sing of these things at random because they have no fear, attributing to a single being the many and varied deeds of them all.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ πολιτείᾳ πλείονι","chosen":"through their higher way of life","rationale":"πολιτεία here denotes conduct or a way of life, and the following section explicitly says that the angels intended to demonstrate the possibility of pious conduct. The comparative may alternatively be understood as “more extensive” rather than “higher.”"},{"source_quote":"πορφύρα τε εἰ τύχοι καλλίστη","chosen":"perhaps the most beautiful purple","rationale":"πορφύρα may denote purple material or dye, while εἰ τύχοι introduces it as a possible example, literally “if it should happen.”"},{"source_quote":"ἀφοβίας αἰτίᾳ ὡς ἔτυχεν ᾄδουσιν","chosen":"sing of these things at random because they have no fear","rationale":"ἀφοβία literally denotes fearlessness but can imply brazen audacity here; ὡς ἔτυχεν means without careful discrimination, “as it happens” or “at random.”"},{"source_quote":"ἐνὶ τοίνυν τὰς πάντων πολλὰς καὶ διαφόρους πράξεις ἀπονέμοντες","chosen":"attributing to a single being the many and varied deeds of them all","rationale":"ἐνί means “to one”; “being” is supplied only to make the otherwise unspecified singular referent intelligible in English."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"8.13","text":"However, when by becoming these things they had exposed as greedy those who seized them, they changed themselves into human nature so that, after living piously and showing that such conduct was possible, they might subject the ungrateful to an accounting. But because they truly became human in every respect and acquired human desire, they were overcome by it and slipped into intercourse with women. Once entangled with them, made fast by defilement, and completely emptied of their original power, they were not strong enough to recombine the members that had been transformed from fire into the original, undefiled state of their own nature. For under the weight produced by desire, their fire ended in flesh, and they traveled the impious road downward. Fettered by bonds of flesh, they have been held down and tightly bound; for this reason they could no longer ascend into the heavens.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπειδὴ ὄντως τὰ πάντα ἄνθρωποι ἐγίνοντο","chosen":"because they truly became human in every respect","rationale":"The accusative τὰ πάντα functions adverbially, indicating complete rather than merely apparent participation in human nature."},{"source_quote":"μιασμῷ παγέντες","chosen":"made fast by defilement","rationale":"παγέντες evokes being fixed, congealed, or solidified. “Made fast” preserves that physical image without deciding whether the author specifically imagines bodily congealing."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἐκ πυρὸς τραπέντα μέλη εἰς τὸ πρῶτον αὐτῶν τῆς ἰδίας φύσεως ἀμίαντον· μετασυγκρῖναι","chosen":"to recombine the members that had been transformed from fire into the original, undefiled state of their own nature","rationale":"μετασυγκρῖναι concerns rearranging or recombining a constitution, not merely changing outward form. The supplied punctuation separates ἀμίαντον from the infinitive, but the syntax still supports taking the phrase as the state into which the members could no longer be restored."},{"source_quote":"τῷ γὰρ βάρει τῷ ὑπὸ τῆς ἐπιθυμίας εἰς σάρκα τελευτήσαντος αὐτῶν τοῦ πυρός","chosen":"For under the weight produced by desire, their fire ended in flesh","rationale":"The weight is most naturally understood as arising from desire and causing the fiery nature to terminate in flesh. The attachment could alternatively be expressed, “when their fire had ended in flesh because of desire, its weight…”"},{"source_quote":"κατέσχηνται","chosen":"have been held down","rationale":"The unusual perfect form is defensibly understood from κατέχω, “hold, restrain.” In context it parallels “fettered” and “tightly bound.”"}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"8.14","text":"After intercourse, when they were asked for what they had become at first and were no longer able to furnish it—because after defilement they could not turn themselves into anything else—and because they wished to please their beloved women, they showed them, in place of themselves, the marrows of the earth, by which I mean the blooms from mines: gold, copper, silver, iron, and the like, together with all the most precious stones. So, along with these enchanted stones, they also handed down the crafts needed for the operations connected with each; they disclosed practices of magic, taught astronomy, the powers of roots, and whatever could never be discovered by human thought, and furthermore the casting of gold, silver, and similar materials, as well as the many-colored dyeing of garments. Simply put, everything that serves women’s adornment and pleasure is an invention of the demons bound in flesh.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὃ τὸ πρῶτον ἐγίνοντο ἀπαιτηθέντες","chosen":"when they were asked for what they had become at first","rationale":"The request concerns their former transformations into precious materials, which they could no longer reproduce after their defilement."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς τῆς γῆς μυελοὺς","chosen":"the marrows of the earth","rationale":"The literal anatomical image is retained and immediately explained by the author as metals and precious stones extracted from mines."},{"source_quote":"οὖν τούτοις δὲ τοῖς μαγευθεῖσιν λίθοις","chosen":"So, along with these enchanted stones","rationale":"All three dative masculine plural forms naturally agree as one noun phrase, and the dative can mark accompaniment or addition. An alternative analysis takes τοῖς μαγευθεῖσιν substantivally and λίθοις instrumentally: “to those bewitched by stones.”"},{"source_quote":"τὰς τέχνας τῶν πρὸς ἕκαστα πραγμάτων","chosen":"the crafts needed for the operations connected with each","rationale":"The compressed phrase refers to technical arts associated with working or using the materials just listed; “each” may refer to each material or to each corresponding operation."},{"source_quote":"πάνθ’ ἁπλῶς ὅσαπερ πρὸς κόσμου καὶ τέρψεώς ἐστι γυναικῶν","chosen":"Simply put, everything that serves women’s adornment and pleasure","rationale":"κόσμος here means ornament or adornment rather than the physical world."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"8.15","text":"From their illegitimate union came illegitimate humans, far taller in stature than human beings, whom later people called giants. They were not serpent-footed or engaged in war against God, as the blasphemous myths of the Greeks sing, but were beastlike in character—larger than humans in size, since they came from angels, yet smaller than angels, since they had been born from women. God therefore knew that they had grown savage to the point of brutishness and that the world was not sufficient to satisfy them, for it had been created in proportion to human beings and for human use. So that they might not seem free from accountability when, through lack of food, they turned to the unnatural eating of animals, on the grounds that they had dared this from necessity, almighty God rained down upon them manna suited to every variety of desire, and they enjoyed everything they wanted. But because of their illegitimate nature, they were not pleased with the purity of the food and craved only the taste of blood. That is why they were the first to taste flesh.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐκ δὲ τῆς νόθου μίξεως αὐτῶν ἄνθρωποι ἐγένοντο νόθοι","chosen":"From their illegitimate union came illegitimate humans","rationale":"Repeating “illegitimate” preserves the author’s repeated νόθος. “Hybrid” or “mixed” could express their composite origin but would weaken the source’s judgment on the union."},{"source_quote":"πολλῷ γε τῶν ἀνθρώπων κατὰ κορυφὴν μείζους","chosen":"far taller in stature than human beings","rationale":"κατὰ κορυφήν concerns height or stature, literally in relation to the head. “Taller by a head” is possible but may impose an exact measurement not required by the phrase."},{"source_quote":"ἀνεύθυνοι δοκῶσιν εἶναι","chosen":"they might not seem free from accountability","rationale":"ἀνεύθυνος denotes exemption from being called to account, not necessarily moral innocence in a broader sense."},{"source_quote":"μάννα αὐτοῖς ὁ παντοδύναμος θεὸς ἐπώμβρισεν ἐκ ποικίλης ἐπιθυμίας","chosen":"almighty God rained down upon them manna suited to every variety of desire","rationale":"The following clause says that they enjoyed whatever they wanted, supporting the sense that the manna answered their varied appetites."},{"source_quote":"σαρκῶν ἐγεύσαντο","chosen":"taste flesh","rationale":"The plural σαρκῶν refers to animal flesh as food. “Meat” would be idiomatic, but “flesh” retains the source’s bodily image and its connection with the preceding taste of blood."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μόνης τῆς τῶν αἱμάτων γεύσεως ἐγλίχοντα.","issue":"As printed, ἐγλίχοντα does not provide the required finite verb for the plural subject οἱ and is not a grammatical form of γλίχομαι in this construction. The translation “craved” therefore depends on a conjectural correction of the final letter rather than on a fully defensible parsing of the supplied form.","proposed_reading":"μόνης τῆς τῶν αἱμάτων γεύσεως ἐγλίχοντο.","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
